cite_portugaise_page.hero_subtitle: The UNESCO-fortified ensemble — gates, walls and the urban core that makes El Jadida unique on the Atlantic.
cite_portugaise_page.overview.title: Mazagan as a whole
cite_portugaise_page.overview.p1: The Portuguese City — still often called Mazagan — is the fortified heart of El Jadida and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Ramparts, gates, the cistern and the dense streets inside form one ensemble.
cite_portugaise_page.overview.p2: Treat it as a walkable district rather than a single monument. Start at the cistern, climb to the Bastion of the Angel, then lose an hour in the lanes.
cite_portugaise_page.overview.p3: This is Atlantic fortress heritage, not inland medina fantasy: stone, wind and sea define the mood.

cite_portugaise_page.faq.title: Portuguese City (Mazagan) FAQ
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q1.question: Is the whole city UNESCO listed?
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q1.answer: The Portuguese City (Mazagan) is the listed fortified ensemble.
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q2.question: One ticket for everything?
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q2.answer: The cistern has its own ticket; wall walks are generally open.
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q3.question: How long for a first visit?
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q3.answer: Half a day covers the highlights without rushing.
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q4.question: Guided tour useful?
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q4.answer: Yes if you want military and trade history in detail.
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q5.question: Best photo spots?
cite_portugaise_page.faq.q5.answer: Cistern interior and the Bastion of the Angel toward the ocean.
